metadata.title: Edge Vision Reliability Lab
metadata.objective: How much can we compress a computer vision model before it becomes unreliable under realistic image degradation, and what trade-offs exist between model size, inference latency, resource consumption, and predictive reliability?
metadata.hardware: Apple M3 (8-core CPU: 4P + 4E, 8 GB Unified Memory)
metadata.evaluation_description: 1,860,000 model-image prediction evaluations (6 model configurations × 31 conditions × 10,000 test images)

resnet18.name: ResNet-18
resnet18.description: Dense residual baseline with standard residual blocks and skip connections

mobilenet_v3_small.name: MobileNetV3-Small
mobilenet_v3_small.description: Compact mobile architecture with depthwise separable convolutions and squeeze-and-excitation blocks

mobilenet_cpu_b1_speedup.label: Single-Image CPU Quantization Speedup
mobilenet_cpu_b1_speedup.device: CPU (Apple M3: 4 threads default vs 1 thread isolated)
mobilenet_cpu_b1_speedup.comparison_type: Deployment-path comparison (FP32 Eager vs INT8 TorchScript/QNNPACK)
mobilenet_cpu_b1_speedup.scope_note: Specific to this Apple M3 CPU benchmark; deployment-path comparison, not pure precision-only scaling.

keyFindings.title: In Evaluated Conditions, FP16 Maintained Predictive Accuracy with ~50% Storage Reduction
keyFindings.summary: In the evaluated benchmark conditions, half-precision conversion achieved a 2.00× serialized reduction for ResNet-18 (44.8 MB → 22.4 MB) and 1.97× for MobileNetV3-Small (6.2 MB → 3.2 MB) without substantial accuracy loss. Measured ResNet-18 clean accuracy was unchanged at 94.78% (99.99% concordance; 1 prediction change out of 10,000), while MobileNetV3-Small changed by 0.02 pp (86.51% → 86.49%, 99.94% concordance).

keyFindings.title: Measurements Show Architecture-Dependent INT8 Quantization Trade-offs
keyFindings.summary: In the evaluated conditions, post-training static quantization (INT8) exhibited asymmetric effects across architectures. Dense ResNet-18 measured a slight clean accuracy delta of +0.03 pp (94.78% → 94.81%, 99.64% concordance), whereas inverted-residual MobileNetV3-Small measured a -0.33 pp delta (86.51% → 86.18%, 95.47% concordance). In CPU latency benchmarks on the Apple M3, the MobileNet batch-1 deployment-path comparison (FP32 Eager vs INT8 TorchScript/QNNPACK) showed a 44.9× latency ratio under default 4-thread execution (25.821 ms vs 0.575 ms) and a 9.1× ratio under isolated single-thread execution (3.78 ms vs 0.41 ms), reflecting that INT8 latency varied less across tested thread configurations while measured FP32 latency was substantially higher under the default four-thread configuration. For ResNet-18, the measured speedup was 1.12× (3.950 ms vs 3.528 ms) under default threading. The benchmark establishes these empirical differences for these deployment paths on this hardware, but does not independently identify underlying causes or generalize to other devices.
keyFindings.evidence: Measured INT8 clean acc delta: ResNet +0.03 pp, MobileNet -0.33 pp; CPU deployment-path ratio: MobileNet 44.9× (4-th) / 9.1× (1-th).

keyFindings.title: Observed Robustness Crossover Under JPEG Compression
keyFindings.summary: Under the evaluated JPEG compression transformations, MobileNetV3-Small recorded higher mean corrupted accuracy than ResNet-18 (69.66% vs 67.83%, a +1.83 pp difference), despite having 7.3× fewer parameters and an 8.27 pp lower clean accuracy baseline. While the measurements establish this empirical crossover under the tested JPEG compression suite, they do not identify the specific architectural factors responsible for the difference.
keyFindings.evidence: Observed JPEG mean corrupted accuracy: MobileNet 69.66% vs ResNet 67.83%.

keyFindings.title: Measurements Show Largest Accuracy Degradation Under Additive Gaussian Noise
keyFindings.summary: Across the six evaluated synthetic corruption types, additive Gaussian noise was accompanied by the largest observed accuracy reduction for both architectures, with measured drops of 49.32 pp on ResNet-18 (from 94.78% clean to 45.46% mean corrupted) and 43.97 pp on MobileNetV3-Small (from 86.51% clean to 42.54% mean corrupted). In contrast, under photometric brightness darkening (factors [0.30, 0.90]), measured accuracy drops were smallest among tested conditions (ResNet dropped 4.12 pp to 90.66%; MobileNet dropped 9.83 pp to 76.68%). In these experiments, measured accuracy degradation was greatest under additive Gaussian noise and least severe under brightness darkening across both architectures.
keyFindings.evidence: Measured Gaussian noise drops: ResNet 49.32 pp, MobileNet 43.97 pp; brightness drops: ResNet 4.12 pp, MobileNet 9.83 pp.

keyFindings.title: Empirical Pareto Frontier on Size-Robustness Plane Consists of INT8 Variants
keyFindings.summary: Under multi-objective evaluation across serialized artifact size versus mean corrupted accuracy across all 30 conditions, the empirical Pareto frontier in this benchmark is formed by the INT8 variants. MobileNetV3-Small INT8 occupied the compact edge boundary (1.94 MB artifact size, 59.01% mean corrupted accuracy), while ResNet-18 INT8 defined the higher-accuracy boundary (11.30 MB artifact size, 65.76% mean corrupted accuracy). Under these benchmark metrics, neither FP32 nor FP16 variants provided a superior combination of smaller disk footprint and higher mean corrupted accuracy.
keyFindings.evidence: Empirical size vs corrupted accuracy frontier: MobileNet INT8 (1.94 MB, 59.01%) and ResNet INT8 (11.30 MB, 65.76%).

methodologyLimitations.title: Custom Synthetic Suite vs Official CIFAR-10-C
methodologyLimitations.detail: The 6 custom synthetic transformations (Gaussian noise, Gaussian blur, horizontal motion blur, brightness darkening, contrast attenuation, and JPEG compression) do not constitute the official CIFAR-10-C 15-corruption benchmark. Metrics reflect perturbation stability under controlled mathematical transformations and cannot be equated with official mean Corruption Error (mCE).

methodologyLimitations.title: 1D Horizontal Motion Blur
methodologyLimitations.detail: Motion blur is evaluated using linear 1D horizontal convolution kernels without directional variance, camera trajectory modeling, or rolling shutter artifacts.

methodologyLimitations.title: Darkening-Only Photometric Shift
methodologyLimitations.detail: The brightness transformation applies scalar intensity attenuation (factors in range [0.30, 0.90]: 0.90, 0.75, 0.60, 0.45, 0.30), modeling underexposure and illumination loss without simulating high-key lighting, glare, or sensor saturation.

methodologyLimitations.title: Resolution & Generalization Scope
methodologyLimitations.detail: All evaluations operate on CIFAR-10's 32×32 spatial resolution with a single fixed training seed (42). Results demonstrate algorithmic sensitivity to resolution-scaled degradations and do not assert real-world out-of-distribution generalization to megapixel industrial camera sensors or autonomous driving feeds.

methodologyLimitations.title: Device & Precision Runtime Disparity
methodologyLimitations.detail: INT8 inference executes strictly on CPU via the QNNPACK backend, while FP16 was evaluated on Apple Silicon MPS. Hardware acceleration characteristics and memory topologies differ fundamentally across these execution targets.

methodologyLimitations.title: Single-Image CPU Threading & Hardware Scope
methodologyLimitations.detail: The 44.9× (default 4 threads) and 9.1× (isolated 1 thread) batch-1 comparisons for MobileNetV3-Small evaluate specific deployment paths (FP32 PyTorch Eager vs INT8 TorchScript/QNNPACK) on Apple M3 CPU. The benchmark establishes these empirical latency differences but does not independently identify their underlying runtime or microarchitectural causes. Results are specific to this Apple M3 benchmark and should not be generalized to other devices or microarchitectures.

gaussian_noise.name: Gaussian Noise
gaussian_noise.description: Additive zero-mean Gaussian noise simulating sensor read noise and low-light electronic grain.

gaussian_blur.name: Gaussian Blur
gaussian_blur.description: Isotropic 2D Gaussian filter simulating optical defocus and lens aberration.

motion_blur.name: Horizontal Motion Blur
motion_blur.description: Linear horizontal 1D convolution kernel simulating fast lateral camera transit or object movement.

brightness.name: Brightness (Darkening)
brightness.description: Multiplicative darkening intensity scaling factor simulating underexposure and progressive illumination drop.

contrast.name: Contrast Attenuation
contrast.description: Linear contrast attenuation relative to per-channel spatial mean simulating atmospheric haze.

jpeg_compression.name: JPEG Compression
jpeg_compression.description: Discrete cosine transform lossy quantization simulating bandwidth-constrained transmission artifacts.
